If any of these already-created custom animations fits better than a standard topic, use it instead by setting "libraryAnimation" to its exact name below (keep "topic" set too, so a sensible daily rhythm can still be estimated):
Ask me about anything – I\'ve grouped it by topic.
What happens when I tap the clock?

It switches to a full-screen bedside display – handy on a nightstand, but the screen stays continuously on while it\'s active, which uses noticeably more battery than usual. Tap anywhere to leave it again.
How is a reminder actually built?

Every reminder has four parts: what to do, a time window (like 8am–8pm), how often I nudge you inside that window, and – optionally – a daily goal. The nudges themselves don\'t count toward anything; only how many times you actually feed me inside your goal does.
What\'s the difference between the interval and the daily goal?

The interval is just how often I tap you on the shoulder – it can be as tight as every minute. The daily goal is what actually counts: set it to 4 and 4 of 4 is done, no matter how many extra nudges I gave you in between.
What does the time window do?
I only nudge you inside that window, e.g. 9am–5pm. Outside it, that reminder stays completely quiet, even once its interval would technically be due again.
Why are my \"open duration\" choices limited?
They only go up to the reminder\'s own interval – one that nudges you every minute can only stay open up to a minute. That way it can never still be sitting there once its own next nudge is due.
What happens when two reminders are due at the same moment?

I show them one after another instead of merging them or moving either one to a different time – whichever has the shorter interval goes first. You\'ll see them appear back-to-back rather than exactly on their own schedule.
What happens if I don\'t feed a reminder right away?

It stays open for as long as its \"open duration\" says – never longer than its own interval. While it\'s open and unfed, though, I don\'t check on any OTHER reminders at all, so it can still hold up whatever else is due until you respond or it times out.
Can a reminder just… not show up?

Yes, on purpose. If I was busy with another open reminder and your reminder\'s moment slipped more than about 90 seconds into the past by the time I got back to it, I won\'t show it late – I quietly line it up for its next slot instead. Showing something noticeably late felt worse than skipping it once. A reminder with a long interval and a long open duration is the most likely one to cause this for a more frequent reminder waiting behind it.
Can the same reminder nudge me twice in a row?
No – I never show the same reminder again before its own interval has fully passed, even if something tries to trigger it early.
Why didn\'t I get a nudge even though nothing seemed to be blocking it?
I only nudge you while your screen is on. If it\'s off right when one\'s due, I skip that occurrence instead of saving it for later – same reasoning as above: better honest than stale.
How long does an animation actually play?
Exactly as long as its open duration says – a quick 8-second flash by default, or longer if you\'ve set that. Feeding me always ends it early, whatever the setting.
Can I use my own animation instead of the built-in ones?
Yes – pick one from the animation library when creating or editing a reminder. A library animation is shown instead of the topic\'s default one.
How do I actually respond to a reminder?
Drag the clock onto me, or use the feed gesture – that\'s how you tell me you did the thing.
Does every reminder affect your mood?

Only if you\'ve turned that on – it\'s off by default (Settings → Mood affects behaviour), so trying the app out never feels like managing anyone\'s feelings. Switched on, only reminders with an actual daily goal count; leave one at \"No goal\" and it stays a pure nudge either way.
What happens to my reminders if I switch avatar?
Each avatar keeps its own set of reminders. Switching avatar switches which set is active – the others are still there, just paused, waiting for you to switch back.
